statement: The irrationality exponent of π is 2. Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational $`p/q`$ satisfies $`|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}`$. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series $`\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)`$, with angles in radians.
